name: Iceland

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: Flat 22% capital income tax on dividends and realised gains (foreign withholding credited against it); no wealth tax. The portfolio is in the estate: 10% inheritance tax on the estate above a CPI-indexed allowance (ISK 6,789,790 in 2026), spouse exempt.

paths.name: Investment holding company (ehf.)
paths.note: An Icelandic ehf. owned by the parents deducts dividends from and gains on shares of qualifying (OECD-rate) companies, so the portfolio is taxed at about 0% inside the company; foreign withholding is lost; payouts to the owners bear 22%. The ehf. shares are in the estate at value, taxed like any asset (no business relief for investment assets was found).

checks.working: Capital income of an individual not in business is taxed at a flat 22% (Income Tax Act No. 90/2003 as applied by Skatturinn, Helstu tolur 2026). Dividends 100,000,000 x 22% = 22,000,000, less the 15% foreign withholding credited under the treaty (resident individuals can credit foreign tax; PwC) 15,000,000, which is below the Icelandic tax on that income: 7,000,000. Gains on foreign listed shares 50,000,000 x 22% = 11,000,000 (no indexation, no holding-period relief). Total 18,000,000. The ISK 600,000 couple's allowance on dividends and listed-share gains (Skatturinn) is ignored as negligible. No wealth tax.

Company tax is 20%, but dividends received from foreign companies are deductible when their profits were taxed abroad at a rate not lower than the general rate in any OECD, EEA or EFTA state, and gains on shares of such companies are deductible in full with 0% tax effect (KPMG, Icelandic Tax Facts 2026, s. 3.7.2 and 3.5.1; PwC Iceland corporate income determination). Assuming the portfolio is listed shares of OECD-resident companies: taxable income from dividends 100,000,000 - 100,000,000 = 0 and from gains 50,000,000 - 50,000,000 = 0, so company tax is 0. The 15,000,000 foreign withholding cannot be credited (no Icelandic tax) and is a cost outside this figure. No annual running cost is recorded in the tax file. Payout tax (22% withheld on distributions to the owners) excluded. No wealth tax.

Inheritance tax is 10% (Act no. 14/2004 art. 2(1)) of the estate's tax base above the tax-free amount, which is ISK 6,789,790 for deaths in 2026 (statutory base ISK 5,000,000 raised in line with consumer prices, art. 2(2); Skatturinn Helstu tolur 2026). It is levied on the estate as a whole whatever the number of heirs, and the tax is on all assets passing to heirs when the estate is divided (art. 1(1)). (1,500,000,000 - 6,789,790) x 10% = 1,493,210,210 x 10% = 149,321,021. The estate passes to the three children, not to a spouse, so the spouse exemption (art. 2(3)) does not apply. Debts and funeral costs ignored.

The parents' ehf. shares are assets passing to the heirs (Act no. 14/2004 art. 1(1)); no relief for an investment company was found. Valued at about the portfolio, the same calculation as for personal holding: (1,500,000,000 - 6,789,790) x 10% = 149,321,021. Unrealised gains inside the company are not taxed at death (no deemed disposal found).

assumptions: Inheritance tax applies to the family's whole estate at the second death, as if the Icelandic estate were settled in Iceland (Act 14/2004 art. 1(1)); the first death to a spouse is exempt (art. 2(3)).
Private foundation and trust are not modelled: Icelandic sjalfseignarstofnun are for declared purposes, not family wealth, and trusts are not an Icelandic legal form.

The holding ehf. is funded with cash or shares at today's value, so no Icelandic tax arises on contributing the portfolio; the portfolio is listed shares of OECD-resident companies held directly, so the dividend and share-gain deductions apply.
Foreign dividends carry 15% withholding; the ISK 600,000 couple's allowance and the 22% top rate apply (no progressive tax on capital income).
open_questions: The ehf. running costs (accounting, audit, directors) are not in the tax file, so the ehf. check counts none.
Whether fund units (ETFs) and emerging-market shares qualify for the company dividend and share-gain deductions was not verified; the article of the Income Tax Act (art. 31) was not opened.
How an ehf.'s shares are valued for inheritance tax (market, book or tax value) was not found; market value is used.
Transferring existing low-cost shares into an ehf. may be a realisation taxable at 22%, or may qualify for a share-exchange roll-over; not verified.
